exercise (long runs and bike rides), you can consume and digest standard
foods while you are working out. Table 10.1 shows several plans for fueling.
Research involving cyclists suggests that Sport Beans, sports drinks, and
gels all offer similar performance benefits (Campbell et al. 2007). Your body
also doesn't care whether you ingest solid or liquid carbohydrate; both
are equally effective (Mason, McConell, and Hargreaves 1993). Even sugar
can be a positive snack during exercise (see chapter 6). The key is to eat
enough carbohydrate: 60 to 90 grams (240 to 360 calories) is more than
many endurance athletes would ever consider ingesting. (Refer to table 6.6,
Carbohydrate Content of Common Foods, to learn what 60 to 90 grams
